findings.title: `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False for `SpawnProcess`, skipping `kill()` and `terminate()`
findings.body: Processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which instantiates `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. In Python's `multiprocessing` module, `SpawnProcess` and `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`) are sibling subclasses of `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` always evaluates to `False`. Wrapping `process.kill()` in `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process):` means hung flusher processes are never killed before spawning a replacement in `_ensure_processes_alive` (and `process.terminate()` at line 346 is likewise never called in `join()`). Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess)` instead.

findings.title: `join()` breaks out of the loop on timeout without terminating remaining processes
findings.body: In `join()`, if `deadline` expires during `self.next_step.join(timeout)` or while waiting for an earlier process in `self.processes` to exit, `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the `for` loop immediately. Any subsequent processes in `self.processes` never reach the termination step at the end of the loop body and will keep running in the background (for example, across consumer partition rebalances when Arroyo closes and joins the strategy). The `while process.is_alive() and (deadline is None or deadline > time.time()):` condition already skips waiting once the deadline has passed, so the early `break` should be removed so all remaining live processes are terminated.

findings.title: `submit()` queries cluster-wide Redis memory `num_processes` times per batch
findings.body: `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` queries `INFO memory` across the Redis cluster nodes rather than only for a specific shard key. Calling `buffer.get_memory_info()` in a loop over `self.buffers.values()` on every `submit()` performs `num_processes` redundant synchronous Redis queries on the main consumer thread and maintains `num_processes` extra `SpansBuffer` instances in the parent process. Retaining `self.buffer = buffer` (which already holds all `assigned_shards`) and calling `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` and `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` once avoids the duplicate Redis round-trips.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key `shards` vs `shard` in `SpanFlusher.main`
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is emitted with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}`, whereas `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` (line 185), `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` (line 195), and `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` (line 244) all use the singular tag key `"shard"`.
